home.title: See beyond the pixel
home.intro: Tala X says what can honestly be said about a photo. First, where the file comes from: a camera original, or a copy reprocessed by a platform such as WhatsApp. Then: where and when it was taken, whether it was edited, and whether the time is possible at the place given, from the position of the sun.
home.feature.1: Camera original or copy reprocessed by a platform
home.feature.2: Recorded place, date, time and time zone
home.feature.3: Editing software recorded in the file
home.feature.4: Position of the sun at the place and time given

analyzing.title: Analysing
analyzing.wait: This takes a few seconds. The report will appear here.
analyzing.deleted: The file will be deleted from the server as soon as the analysis ends. Nothing is kept.
legend.title: How to read the report
legend.intro: Each check gets one of these four states, always with its explanation. There is no overall score and no percentage: it is up to you to judge, check by check.
state.to_check.meaning: An anomaly that may have a legitimate explanation.
state.suspicious.meaning: A contradiction that is hard to explain otherwise.
state.unverifiable.meaning: The information needed is missing from the file.
says.title: What Tala X says, and what it does not
says.1: Tala X certifies nothing. “Camera original” means that the file carries the marks of a camera, not that what it shows is true.
says.2: Every result is an indication with its explanation, to be read with your own judgement. Metadata can be forged by someone who knows how.
says.3: Tala X is designed against laundering by platforms and recycled images, not against expert forgers.
report.integrity: Integrity test · origin of the file
report.thumbnail.alt: The preview embedded in the file
report.no_thumbnail: This file holds no embedded preview.
report.image_unavailable: Your browser cannot display this image format. The analysis did examine the file.
report.suspicious: a contradiction to examine before drawing any conclusion.
sky.banner_lead: A question to complete the solar check:
sky.banner_question: what does the photo show: day, twilight or night?
sky.title: What does the photo show?
sky.help: Look at the photo and choose what it shows. Your choice runs the analysis of the same file again: it is sent again, analysed, then deleted, like the first time.
download.note: The server makes the report: the file is sent to it again, then deleted. Changing the language asks for the report again in the same way. The downloaded report opens without a network connection.
map.warning: The area will be requested from OpenStreetMap by our server. OpenStreetMap sees neither your address nor your file.
map.label: Map centred on the recorded position, {position}, with a marker
map.marker: Marker: position recorded in the file, {position}.
map.failed: The map could not be loaded. The analysis itself is not affected.
source.copy_failed: Copying is not possible here: select the message and copy it.
claim.title: Check the caption
claim.lead_missing: The file does not say where or when the photo was taken. Enter the place and time the caption claims: Tala X computes where the sun was, then you say what the photo shows.
claim.lead: Enter the place and time the caption claims: Tala X compares them with the file and with the sun.
claim.offer: The caption places or dates the photo? Check it against the file and the sun.
claim.open: Enter the place and time claimed
claim.place_hint: For example -4.32170, 15.31250. Paste them from a map service, or pick the place on the map.
claim.place_invalid: Write the latitude, then the longitude, in decimal degrees: for example -4.32170, 15.31250.
claim.incomplete: The place, the date and the time are all needed.
claim.note: The place and time are sent with the file, analysed, then deleted like it.
claim.current: Claim entered: {place}, on {date} at {time}, local time.
picker.label: Map: click where the caption says the photo was taken
picker.help: Click where the caption says the photo was taken; the coordinates fill in. A few kilometres off barely change the sun.
weather.title: Cross-check with the weather
weather.lead: Tala X asks the Open-Meteo weather model what the weather was at the place and time of the photo; then you say what the photo shows.
weather.warning: The place, rounded to about 11 km, and the date will be sent to Open-Meteo by our server. Open-Meteo may keep them in its logs for 90 days. It receives neither your address nor your file. For a sensitive file, do not do it.
weather.needs_claim: A place and a time are needed first: enter those of the caption above.
weather.question: What weather does the photo show?
weather.question_help: Choose what you see. Your choice runs the analysis of the same file again, and the weather is asked again.
weather.banner_lead: A question to complete the weather check:
weather.banner_question: what weather does the photo show?
